title: Three-channel anticommutator bridge for half-density modular tails
question: Can the Gibbs half-density anticommutator and commutator costs be decomposed into left/right GNS legs and a positive beta/2 two-slice cross term, so the unresolved modular tail is separated into independently controllable channels?
method: Use the actual-Q3 edge and square finite fixtures with all translated sites and bond terms, both term orders, both time signs, every prefix position and both history adjoints on the declared cutoffs.
Diagonalize each doubled bond generator, construct rho^(1/2) and rho^(1/4), and center every moved Hermitian witness in the same bond-Gibbs state.
Compute L=||rho^(1/2)X||_2^2, R=||X rho^(1/2)||_2^2, T=||rho^(1/4)Xrho^(1/4)||_2^2, and check the commutator, anticommutator and sum decompositions together with T<=(L+R)/2.
Reconstruct the same grid without importing the primary audit and compile the scalar channel identities and arithmetic--geometric envelope in Lean R379.
finding: The primary lane passes 23050/23050 assertions and the non-importing independent lane passes 8/8 aggregate assertions over 2560 all-prefix contexts. The integrated verifier passes 69/69 and Lean R379 compiles. The largest left and right legs are 41.6482665166188, the largest two-slice leg is 41.57042344053425, the largest commutator leg is 0.5097575476240509, and the largest anticommutator leg is 166.281693762137. The two-slice fraction reaches 1.0000000000000004 at roundoff, so the cross term cannot be discarded. Primary and independent values agree within 5.684e-13.
decision_reason: The three-channel identity turns the R-378 anticommutator into two explicit GNS legs plus a beta/2 Euclidean two-slice leg. The finite data identify the two-slice channel as the dominant unresolved cost while the commutator leg remains small on the tested grid. This is a route-local decomposition, not a uniform estimate or a QFT promotion.

adversarial_review.check: The anticommutator uses +2T and the commutator uses -2T, both checked from direct matrix products.
The two-slice term uses rho^(1/4) on both sides of X; no one-sided surrogate is substituted.
Direct products and spectral sums are compared without commuting rho, its roots or X.
The cross estimate is one-sided T<=(L+R)/2 and finite saturation is retained.
All Hilbert--Schmidt squares and the two-slice leg are checked nonnegative, including zero-commutator rows.
Every channel uses the same bond-Gibbs centered witness; centering is not moved through the Gibbs factors.
The edge cutoff-6 costs remain large, so no cutoff or volume uniformity is inferred.
The density is a finite doubled-bond proxy, not a thermodynamic KMS state or OS reconstruction.
The independent lane rebuilds oscillator, graph, spectrum, prefixes and three products without importing the primary audit.
No modular tail, common core, common alpha, KMS/GNS dynamics, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A conclusion is drawn.

next_action: Prove a beta/2 Euclidean two-slice tail estimate on the Hamiltonian-derived core, then combine it with left/right GNS bounds and the R-378 geometric shell and R-377 resolvent telescope.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite three-channel half-density interface only. It does not prove source/volume/cutoff/beta uniformity, modular tails, common core, common alpha, KMS/GNS dynamics, a gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A.
no_overclaim: R-379 identifies the dominant finite two-slice channel; it is not a uniform theorem or a QFT closure.
